about:
Miami Woodworking has operated in Lebanon, Ohio for nearly 30 years. The business was founded by Ken and his wife Phyllis, whose warmth and care became the foundation of the company. The shop is identified as a family-owned woodworking shop, and Phyllis’s legacy is highlighted as a guiding influence.

The company functions as a full custom woodworking shop, providing design, fabrication, and installation services. Its capabilities include custom cabinetry for kitchens and baths, built-in bookcases and media walls, wine cellars and racks, distressed timber beams and mantels, entertainment centers, and exotic solid-wood bar tops and countertops. All work is produced in their Lebanon facility, and the firm emphasizes a start-to-finish design process that covers planning, measuring, material selection, and project completion.

Miami Woodworking serves residential clients throughout the region, as well as commercial projects such as bars and wine rooms. Typical projects include built-in mud benches, home offices, and architectural woodwork for entire homes. The company works directly with homeowners, designers, and contractors who require tailored millwork.

The firm distinguishes itself by positioning its service as an alternative to big-box retailers, stating that custom woodworking is its sole focus. It promotes a designer-led approach where a single point of contact manages the project from concept to installation, and it cites nearly three decades of experience in architectural woodwork as a mark of reliability.

about:
Michelsen Packaging Co. was founded in 1937 in Fresno, California, as a manufacturer and distributor of protective packaging for fresh produce. The company remains privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed. Its founder established a philosophy of exceptional customer service that continues to guide operations.

The company produces a range of packaging materials including Jiffy® macerated produce pads, Kushion Kraft®, Bubble Wrap®, Cell-Aire® polyethylene foam, embossed tissue, diaper pads, and soaker pads. It also manufactures raisin trays under the SUN-DRY® and SUNBEAM® brands and continuous raisin paper rolls. Michelsen describes itself as the valley’s oldest and largest manufacturer and distributor of these products, though facility size and headcount are not published.

Primary customers are growers, packers, and shippers of fresh fruits and vegetables such as peaches, plums, nectarines, apricots, apples, pears, grapes, asparagus, and berries. The company also serves the raisin industry with tray and roll products. Its market focus is the Central Valley agricultural sector.

Michelsen cites its founder’s credo — “Exceptional customer service continues as our number one goal” — as the principle that differentiates it. The firm also notes its status as the “#1 choice of valley growers for Continuous Raisin Paper Rolls.”

name: Michigan Food Equipment Co
old_description: • Experience Cutting-Edge technology  that revolutionizes Bacon slicing with  unmatched accuracy.
about:
Michigan Food Equipment Co is based in Howell, Michigan. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It operates as a manufacturer of food processing equipment, with a focus on bacon slicing and interleaving systems.

The company designs and builds the Razorback line of industrial bacon slicers and paper interleavers. Its slicers feature variable blade speeds up to 1,650 rpm and claim production rates up to 4,000 pounds per hour, with thickness regulation and waste-slice elimination. Michigan Food Equipment also rebuilds used industrial meat packaging equipment and manufactures replacement parts in-house, including components for Anco presses and slicers.

The equipment serves meat and food processing plants, particularly bacon and sliced-meat producers. Customers include operations seeking to integrate slicing and interleaving into existing production lines, as well as those needing rebuilt machinery or spare parts for legacy Anco systems.

The company emphasizes domestic parts manufacturing and the ability to service equipment worldwide, positioning itself as a single source for both new machinery and ongoing support.

name: Michigan Freeze Pack Co
old_description: Michigan Freeze Pack is a leading processor of Frozen Vegetables for the ingredient industry. Located in Hart, Michigan – the premiere growing region for vegetables.
about:
Michigan Freeze Pack operates from Hart, Michigan, in the heart of the state's prime vegetable-growing region. The company was established in 1988 as a grower-owned cooperative and remains a multi-generational family enterprise. Its farmer-owners built the facility to process vegetables grown on their own lands, creating a direct link between field and freezer.

The 100,000-square-foot plant specializes in individually quick frozen (IQF) vegetables for the ingredient market. Core products include asparagus, butternut squash, cabbage, carrots, celery, green zucchini, potatoes, and yellow zucchini. The operation offers custom processing, blending, packing, and cold storage, and can also contract-grow specific varieties for customers who meet volume thresholds. Clients may supply their own raw material for toll processing.

Michigan Freeze Pack serves food ingredient manufacturers and distributors who require consistent, specification-driven frozen vegetables. Its customer base includes companies that incorporate IQF vegetables into prepared meals, soups, sauces, and retail frozen blends. The USDA-inspected facility supports both conventional and organic production lines.

The grower-owned structure is central to the company's value proposition: it enables a "Grown and Processed in the USA" claim, ensures traceability from seed to package, and aligns with sustainable farming practices. The cooperative model also allows rapid response to customer specifications while maintaining the environmental stewardship the founding families prioritize.

about:
Micro Mold Plastics USA, Inc. operates from Fort Worth, Texas. The current woman-owned entity began production in March 2018 under president Lisa K. Allison, though its lineage traces back to Micro Molding Inc. in the 1960s and Micro Mold Plastics Inc., established in 1987.

The company specializes in small, close-tolerance injection molding from a 20,000-square-foot facility equipped with presses ranging from 25 to 240 tons. Core processes include injection molding, close-tolerance molding, sonic welding, and hot stamping, supported by in-house testing and inspection.

Micro Mold Plastics serves customers requiring precision plastic components, with its AS9100D certification and DDTC registration indicating work in aerospace and defense markets. The firm emphasizes quality parts and superior customer service, drawing on a combined 120-plus years of industry experience among its team.

Founded to provide quality parts paired with responsive service, the company leverages its deep plastics heritage and certified quality system to meet tight-tolerance demands.

about:
Microboard Processing, Inc. was founded in 1983 by Craig Hoekenga in Seymour, Connecticut. Before entering electronics manufacturing, Hoekenga had built a national reputation as an efficiency consultant to companies such as GE, GTE, Panasonic, IBM, and Phillips. Today the company is woman-owned, led by President and CEO Nicole Russo.

The firm provides electronics manufacturing services including circuit card assembly, system integration, and test services. It emphasizes high-reliability, high-complexity manufacturing with a focus on rigorous testing and quality. Microboard operates with a strong engineering staff, a dedicated RF test design team, and leading-edge equipment and software capable of placing the industry’s smallest components to build complex, fail-critical boards.

Microboard serves the defense, medical, telecommunications, and industrial sectors. Its customer base ranges from government contractors to innovative startups, with the company stating a focus on “life saving and life changing products.”

The company’s guiding principles—Process Excellence, Partnership, and People—underpin a self-described “zero defect culture of continuous improvement” and a motto of “brilliant together.” Microboard also highlights its commitment to humanitarian work, including wells, food, and medicine for marginalized communities, as an inseparable part of its culture.

name: Micron Semiconductor Products Inc.
old_description: Welcome to Micron.com, please Log in or Register an account to continue.
about:
Micron Semiconductor Products Inc. is headquartered in Meridian, Idaho. The company traces its origins to 1978, when a four-person team launched a semiconductor design venture in the basement of a Boise, Idaho dental office. By 1980, the founders had broken ground on their first fabrication plant, and within a few years they introduced the world’s smallest 256K DRAM. The business went public and joined the Fortune 500 in 1994, growing through technology innovations, partnerships, and strategic acquisitions into a global memory and storage manufacturer.

Today Micron designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of memory and storage products, including DRAM components and modules, LPDDR, GDDR, NAND flash, NOR flash, managed NAND, multichip packages, and solid-state drives for data center, client, automotive, and industrial markets. The company operates multiple fabrication facilities and oversees wafer fabrication, assembly, test, and packaging processes. Recent milestones include high-volume production of HBM4 for NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform and mass production of its sixth-generation PCIe Gen6 SSD, alongside a 245TB data-center SSD now shipping.

Micron serves customers across automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, data center and cloud, client PC, consumer electronics, mobile, network infrastructure, industrial IoT, robotics, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and video security sectors. Its products are used by original equipment manufacturers, system integrators, hyperscale data-center operators, and automotive Tier 1 suppliers who require high-reliability memory for demanding environments.

The company was founded to advance semiconductor memory technology and has consistently focused on innovation that transforms how information is used. Micron states its purpose is to enrich life for all by delivering optimal memory and storage systems for a wide range of applications, from AI and the cloud to the intelligent edge.

name: Mid-South Medical Imaging, LLC
old_description: Mid-South Medical Imaging, LLC is the oldest and largest independent medical imaging company in our area.
about:
Mid-South Medical Imaging, LLC, originally founded as Mid-South X-Ray in 1968, is headquartered in Flowood, Mississippi. The company operates additional branches in Birmingham, Alabama, and Memphis, Tennessee, serving healthcare providers across Mississippi, Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, western Tennessee, and the Florida panhandle.

The company distributes a broad range of medical imaging equipment, including digital radiography rooms and portables, R/F systems, radiology and point-of-care ultrasound, CT, MRI, mammography, and C-arm systems. It carries thousands of healthcare products from manufacturers such as Adaptix and Samsung, and employs registered x-ray technologists who provide applications training for the equipment it sells. Service capabilities include phone and email support as well as remote support technology for rapid troubleshooting.

Mid-South Medical Imaging primarily serves hospitals, orthopedic practices, and women's health facilities. Its product lineup features the Adaptix Ortho350 portable 3D orthopedic imaging system, the Samsung R20 AI-powered general imaging ultrasound, and the Samsung GM85 Fit mobile X-ray unit. The company also supplies 3D mammography, upright stereotactic biopsy, and breast ultrasound workstations for women's health programs.

The company emphasizes "Southern service, digital-age support," highlighting its focus on quality customer relations and post-sale service. Its remote support technology allows the service team to resolve issues quickly without on-site visits, a capability the company says sets it apart in the region.
